questions.question: Who was the first to develop a mathematical predictive heliocentric model of the solar system?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Nicolaus Copernicus.__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Nicolaus Copernicus (1473 - 1543) was born in Kingdom of Poland.
 
• Nicolaus work **"De revolutionibus orbium coelestium" **(On the Revolutions of the Celestial Spheres), gives the information about heliocentric model.
 
• it provided information that **the Sun in centre of Universe and rotation of Planets around the sun**.
 
• It was **published in 1543,** the year of his death.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• I**mmanuel Kant (1724-1804) **is widely known for modern philosophy.
 
• His important work "**Critique of Practical Reason," **Kant discusses his theory of ethics, including the famous concept of the Categorical Imperative, which is a universal moral law.
 
• He also made contributions** to "Nebular Hypothesis,"** proposing that solar systems develop from rotating clouds of gas, anticipating later theories of stellar and planetary formation.
 
• **Galileo Galilei (1564 - 1642) **was Italain Mathematician, Physicist, and Astronomer
 
• Galileo is famous for his **improvements to the telescope**.
 
• He made contributions to the **study of motion and mechanics, the laws of falling bodies**.
 
• **Pierre Simon - Laplace (1749 - 1827): **was French Mathematician and Astronomer 
 
• He laid the **foundations of statistics and probability** theory.
 
• His work in mathematics led to the development of **Laplace's equation.**
 
• He also developed the **Laplace Nebular Hypothesis** independently of Kant.

questions.question: Name the web portal launched by the Department of Telecommunication sharing information on mobile towers and EMF Emission Compliances.

questions.question: What is the duration of single round in free style wrestling?

• Wrestlers typically compete in **two periods of 3 minutes each** in international competitions.

• **Weight Classes:** Freestyle wrestling has multiple weight classes to ensure fair competition, allowing wrestlers to compete against others of similar size and weight.

questions.question: Which of the following causes enlargement and extension growth of cells?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Turgor pressure.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Enlargement and extension growth of cells is primarily caused by **cell turgor pressure** and **cell wall expansion**.
 
• In plants, this growth is **driven by water uptake**, which increases turgor pressure within the cells, leading to expansion.
 
• Additionally, the synthesis of new cell wall materials allows for **cell elongation.**
 
• Other factors, such as **hormonal regulation** (e.g., auxins), also play a role in promoting cell growth and elongation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Imbibition**

 
 
• It is the process by which a substance (usually a solid, like seeds or plant tissues) **absorbs water and swells.**
 
• This occurs due to the affinity of water molecules for the polar surfaces of the solid. In seeds, imbibition triggers metabolic activities, leading to germination.
 
• **Example**: When dry seeds are placed in water, they absorb water, swell, and become turgid, preparing for germination.
 
 
 
• **Pressure Potential**
 
 
• Pressure potential is the physical pressure exerted by the fluid (usually water) within the cell** against the cell wall.**
 
• In plant cells, when water enters the cell through osmosis, it creates turgor pressure that pushes the plasma membrane against the cell wall, contributing to the overall water potential.
 
• Pressure potential is essential for maintaining cell structure and rigidity, **allowing plants to stand upright and grow.**
 
 
 
• **Osmotic Pressure**
 
 
• It is the pressure required to **prevent the flow of water across a semipermeable membrane **due to osmotic potential (the tendency of water to move into a solution).
 
• It results from differences in solute concentration on either side of a membrane. Water moves from an area of lower solute concentration (higher water potential) to an area of higher solute concentration (lower water potential).
 
• It is crucial for processes like nutrient uptake, cell hydration, and overall water balance in cells and organisms.

questions.question: Which Article provides that all minorities have the right to establish and administer educational institutions of their choice?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 30.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 30** specifically states that all minorities, whether based on religion or language, have the right to establish and administer educational institutions of their choice.
 
• The article not only grants the right to establish educational institutions but also ensures that minorities **can administer these institutions **according to their own management and governance structures. 
 
• Article 30 serves as a **safeguard against any discriminatory policies **that might hinder the establishment or functioning of educational institutions by minorities. 
 
• The Supreme Court of India has elaborated on the scope of Article 30 in various judgments, affirming the right of minorities to manage their institutions without undue interference from the state. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
 

 **Article**
 **Title**
 **Description**
 
 
 
 

 **24**
 **Prohibition of Employment of Children in Factories, etc.**
 Prohibits the employment of children below the age of 14 years in factories, mines, and hazardous jobs, ensuring protection against exploitation.
 
 

 **25**
 **Freedom of Conscience and Free Profession, Practice, and Propagation of Religion**
 Guarantees the right to freedom of conscience and the right to freely profess, practice, and propagate religion, subject to public order, morality, and health.
 
 

 **32**

questions.question:
What happens in case of market equilibrium:

(a) Market demand = market supply

(b) There is no excess supply in the market
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Both (a) and (b).**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The market attains equilibrium when the market supply and market demand of a commodity become equal.
 
• The term supply refers to how much of a certain product, item, commodity, or service suppliers are willing to make available at a particular price
 
• Demand refers to how much of that product, item, commodity, or service consumers are willing and able to purchase at a particular price
 
• Supply and demand are economic forces of the free market that control what suppliers are willing to produce and what consumers are willing and able to purchase.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• If the market price is above the equilibrium value, there is an excess supply in the market (a surplus), which means there is more supply than demand.
 
• If the market price is below the equilibrium value, then there is an excess in demand (supply shortage).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9042c9dca25efe9625d51e525814238bd7e86f2da7945bd56a70fc82bed307ae.png]

questions.question: Which amongst the following statements is correct about Mughal emperor Akbar ?

options.text: He fought and won the third battle of Panipat against the Hindu King Hemu.
He founded a new religion called ‘Din - e Ilahi’.
He was highly educated and knew many languages.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**He founded a new religion called 'Din - e llahi'**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Din - e Ilahi also known as the **"Religion of God"**.
 
• It was founded by The Mughal Emperor, Akbar(1556-1605) **in 1582**.
 
• It has the combined elements of **Islam, Hinduism, Jainism, Christianity and Zoroastrianism.**
 
• Akbar's full name was **"Jalal-ud-din Muhammad Akbar"**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Akbar was the son of Emperor Humayun. Initially, his regent and guardian was **Bairam Khan**.
 
• The third battle of Panipat was fought between the **Maratha Empire** led by** Sadashivrao Bhau** and the** Durrani Empire** led by **Ahmad Shah Durrani**.
 
• The third battle of Panipat was** won by the Durrani Empire** and is known as one of the bloodiest wars of the 18th century.
 
• Akbar did not receive formal education, he could not read or write but could communicate in **Persian, Arabic, and Hindi.**
 
• Akbar established **Ibadat Khana(House of Worship)** for Scholars and Intellectuals in **Fatehpur Sikri**.
 
• Akbar court featured the** Navratnas(Nine Jewels),** a group of talented advisors.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a part of Carnatic music?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Dhrupad**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Dhrupad** is a genre of classical music that is a **part of the Hindustani music tradition**, not Carnatic music.
 
• It is one of the oldest forms of North Indian classical music and has its origins in the ancient text of **Samaveda**.
 
• Dhrupad is characterized by its spiritual, meditative nature and the use of a specific style of singing.
 
• It is distinct from Carnatic music, which is a classical music tradition from South India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Charana**

 
 
• Charana is a part of **Carnatic music** compositions.
 
• It refers to the concluding section of a composition, often following the Pallavi and Anupallavi sections.
 
• This section typically elaborates on the theme introduced in the earlier parts.
 
 
 
• **Pallavi**
 
 
• Pallavi is the thematic line of a song in **Carnatic music**.
 
• It is often the first section of a composition and is usually repeated throughout the song.
 
• Pallavi sets the tone and mood for the entire composition.
 
 
 
• **Varnam**
 
 
• Varnam is a form of song in **Carnatic music**.
 
• It is typically composed in two parts: the Purvanga (first half) and Uttaranga (second half).
 
• Varnams are often used as warm-up pieces and are known for their complexity and technical demands.

questions.question: In MS Word, which option allows you to insert a new column in a table while simultaneously shifting the existing columns to the right ?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 4) Insert Column to the Left**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

In **Microsoft Word**, when working with tables:

 
• **"Insert Column to the Left"** adds a new column **to the left** of the selected cell/column, pushing the existing columns **to the right**.
 
• **"Insert Column to the Right"** (Option 1) adds a new column **to the right**, shifting subsequent columns further right (but does not move the selected column).
 
• **"Insert Table"** (Option 2) is irrelevant—it creates a new table.
 
• **"Insert Columns"** (Option 3) is not a standard option; Word specifies left/right insertion.

**Why Option 4?**

The question asks for inserting a column **while shifting existing columns to the right**, which only happens when inserting **to the left** of a selected column.

 **Correct Choice: Option 4 (Insert Column to the Left)**

questions.question: According to the Census 2011 of India, which metropolitan has the second highest population?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Delhi.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The population of Delhi in 2011 was approximately **16.8 million.**
 
• The metropolitan area with the **highest population** is **Mumbai**, which had a population of about 20.4 million.
 
• The **third largest** metropolitan area was** Kolkata**, with a population of around 14.1 million.
 
• The 2011 Census was the **15th national census** **since 1871** and was conducted in **two phases**—house listing and population enumeration.
 
• The 2011 Census of India was the** 7th national census** conducted **after independence in 1947.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Total Population:
 
 
• India's total population was approximately **1.21 billion** (1,210,854,977).
 
 
 
• Growth Rate:
 
 
• The population **growth rate **from 2001 to 2011 was **17.7%,** a decrease from the previous decade's rate of 21.5%.
 
 
 
• Gender Ratio:
 
 
• The overall sex ratio was **940 females for every 1,000 males**.
 
• Child sex ratio (ages 0-6) was 919 girls for every 1,000 boys.
 
 
 
• Urban vs. Rural:
 
 
• Urban population: **31.16%** (approximately 377 million).
 
• Rural population:** 68.84%** (approximately 833 million).
 
 
 
• Literacy Rate:
 
 
• The national literacy rate was **74.04%.**
 
• **Male literacy: 82.14%; Female literacy: 65.46%.**
 
 
 
• States and Union Territories:
 
 
• **Uttar Pradesh** was the **most populous state**, with over 199 million people.
 
• The **least populous** state was** Sikkim,** with about 610,577 people.
 
 
 
• Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes:
 
 
• **Scheduled Castes**: **16.6%** of the population.
 
• **Scheduled Tribes: 8.6%** of the population.
 
 
 
• Literacy by State:
 
 
• **Kerala** had the **highest literacy** rate at **93.91%**.
 
• **Bihar** had the **lowest literacy rate** at** 61.80%**.

questions.question: Brahmo Samaj was earlier known as :
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Brahmo__ Sabha__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Brahmo Samaj was earlier known as the Brahmo Sabha.
 
• It was founded in**1828 by Raja Ram Mohan Roy** and others as a reform movement within Hinduism.
 
• **Keshab Chandra Sen** expanded the movement in the 1860s and introduced new ideas, forming the **Brahmo Samaj of India in 1866.**
 
• Raja Ram Mohan Roy is known as the **"Father of the Bengal Renaissance".**
 
• He was against the practice of **sati(widow immolation), **which led to the eventual legal ban on the practice in 1829.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Arya Samaj:-**

 
 
• Founded in **1875 by Swami Dayananda Saraswati in Mumbai**, India.
 
• Emphasizes the teachings of the **Vedas **as the ultimate authority in Hinduism.
 
• The organization has published many texts and pamphlets promoting its teachings and reforms, including **Satyarth Prakash (The Light of Truth).**
 
 
 
• **Prarthana Samaj:-**
 
 
• Founded in **1867 in Mumbai** (then Bombay) by** Dr. Atmaram Pandurang** and a group of like-minded individuals.

 Notable members included **M. G. Ranade, Gopal Ganesh Agarkar, and R. G. Bhandarkar**, who contributed to its ideals and initiatives.
 
 
 
• **Veda Samaj:-**
 
 
• Established in **1864 in Madras** (now Chennai) by** S. Ramasamy** (also known as **Veda Vyasar)**.
 
• Aimed to promote a return to the original teachings of the Vedas, emphasizing monotheism and rational spirituality.

questions.question: Which of the following committees recommended the inclusion of fundamental duties in the Constitution of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Swaran Singh Committee.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Swaran Singh Committee recommended the inclusion of Fundamental Duties in the Constitution of India.
 
• The committee was constituted in **1976** by the Indian government to recommend amendments to the Constitution.
 
• The committee proposed that citizens have certain duties towards the nation, which led to the incorporation of** Part IV-A** in the Constitution, containing **Article 51A.**
 
• The recommendations were accepted, and the **Forty-Second Amendment** to the Constitution was enacted in **1976**, officially adding the Fundamental Duties.
 
• The Constitution currently enumerates **11 Fundamental Duties.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Balwant Rai Mehta Committee**:-

 
 
• Established in **1957** by the Government of India to examine and recommend measures for the effective implementation of the Panchayati Raj system.
 
• Led by **Balwant Rai Mehta**, who was a prominent political leader and advocate for local self-governance.
 
• Recommended a **three-tier structure for Panchayati Raj** consisting of:
 
 
• Gram Panchayat (village level)
 
• Panchayat Samiti (block level)
 
• Zila Parishad (district level) 
 
 
 
 
 
• **Raja Mannar Committee:-**
 
 
• Established in **1965 by the Government of Tamil Nadu** to review and recommend reforms in the administration of local self-governments.
 
• **Chaired by Raja Mannar**, a prominent figure known for his contributions to public administration and governance.
 
• Proposed the establishment of a **two-tier system for local self-governance**, consisting of:
 
 
• Village Panchayats
 
• District Panchayats
 
 
 
 
 
• **Sarkaria Committee:-**
 
 
• Established in **1983** by the Government of India to review the relationship between the Centre and the states.
 
• Chaired by **Ranjit Singh Sarkaria**, a former judge of the Supreme Court of India.
 
• Addressed concerns related to the **distribution of powers and responsibilities** between the Centre and the states.
 
• Reviewed the **role of the Governor** in the states and its implications for state autonomy.

questions.question: Which is the waterbody that separates Andaman Islands and Nicobar Islands?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Ten Degree Channel.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Ten Degree Channel is situated between the** Andaman Islands to the north and the Nicobar Islands to the south i**n the Bay of Bengal.
 
• The channel is approximately **150 kilometers wide** at its narrowest point.
 
• The channel plays a **crucial role in maritime navigation**, connecting the Bay of Bengal to the Andaman Sea.
 
• The Ten Degree Channel is a major** trade route** for goods traveling from the** South China Sea and Pacific to the Indian Ocean.**
 
• **Barren Island**, located in the Andaman Islands, is home to** Asia's only active volcano.**
 
• The Andaman and Nicobar Islands are home to 96 wildlife sanctuaries and one biosphere reserve.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• The Nine Degree Channel separates the **Laccadive Islands** to the** west** from the **Malabar Coast** of India to the** east.**
 
• The Eleven Degree Channel lies **south of the Nicobar Islands**, separating them from the **Indonesian islands.**
 
• The Eight Degree Channel is situated between the** Lakshadweep Islands** to the north and the **Maldives** to the south.
 
• The **Great Nicobar Biosphere Reserve** is the only biosphere reserve in the Andaman and Nicobar Islands.
 
• The reserve includes **Galathea National Park and Campbell Bay National Park**.
 
• It was added to** UNESCO's Man and Biosphere Programme in 2013** to promote sustainable development.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The **Man and the Biosphere (MAB) Programme** is a scientific program by UNESCO that aims to improve the **relationship between people and the environment**. 
 
• The program was** launched in 1971** and uses a combination of natural and social sciences to achieve its goals.

questions.question: According to the Department of Industrial Policy and Promotion, which of the following is NOT a core industry?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Jute.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Core industries are crucial for the economy as they provide **essential goods and services.**
 
• The **Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT)** in India considers the following **eight sectors** to be the core industries:
 
 
• cement
 
• coal
 
• crude oil
 
• electricity
 
• fertilizers
 
• natural gas
 
• refinery products
 
• steel
 
 
 
• Industries that are **NOT considered** core industries could include sectors like textiles, consumer goods, or services.
 
• The growth rate of the core sector is a crucial **indicator of the overall health of the Indian economy**.
 
• A **strong growth rate** in the core sector often signals a **positive economic outlook.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The eight core industries make up **40.27%** of the Industrial Production (IIP)'s weight.
 
• The** weightage** of the core industries, in** decreasing order,** is refinery products,** electricity, steel, coal, crude oil, natural gas, cement, and fertilizers.** 
 
• To improve the core sector growth in the country the prominent **measures taken **recently are as follows:
 
 
• The** National Infrastructure Pipeline** is expected to significantly boost infrastructure and spur growth impulses in the economy.
 
• **Infrastructure and housing schemes** that will stimulate the production and sale of cement, steel, and other construction materials resulting in a multiplier effect on the economy:-
 
 
• Make in India
 
• PradhanMantri Gram SadakYojana
 
• PradhanMantriAwaasYojana – Gramin
 
• PM AwaasYojana (Urban)
 
• Swachh Bharat Mission
 
• JalJeevan Mission to provide ‘HarGharJal’ 
 
 
 
• As part of Atmanirbhar Bharat Abhiyan, a **Production Linked Incentive (PLI) scheme** has been announced to enhance the production of **‘Speciality Steel’, **incorporating four different product categories.
 
• The **Integrated Power Development Scheme (IPDS)** has been approved to facilitate state utilities to ensure quality and reliable 24x7 power supply in the urban areas
